sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
South Tyneside's policy is to keep the seafront and town centre of South Shields paying for itself and to ease pressure in residential streets. The council's 2024-25 parking report lists 18 chargeable off-street car parks with 2,145 spaces in South Shields town centre and on the foreshore, 238 chargeable on-street bays and 33 resident permit schemes; it issued 19,788 penalty charge notices in 2024-25, up from 15,282, and says its aims are to support town-centre viability and reduce congestion [0][3]. During 2024-25 the seafront car parks charged 1.20 pounds an hour or 6 pounds all day, and the town centre 1 penny per minute for the first hour and 4 pounds all day [2].

Prices are rising. A notice published on 11 May 2026 said that from 8 June 2026 seafront charges would change from 1.20 to 1.60 pounds an hour and from 6 to 8 pounds all day, and the first hour in the town-centre car parks would become free [4]. A notice of 14 August 2026 lists those as the current charges and says the all-day charge would be 10 pounds on Sunday 13 September 2026, without giving a reason [5]. In June 2026 the council made a parking order bringing pay and display to McAnany Avenue and Station Road, near the hospital, in operation from 15 June 2026; after objections the proposed charges at Mill Dam did not take effect [6][8]. The order also adds contactless payment at machines equipped for it [7]. In December 2025 the council consulted on permit parking around the foreshore, with a first resident permit free for a year; no outcome was found [10]. A proposed Westoe controlled parking zone was dropped for now because residents were mostly opposed [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The development has been in charges and enforcement more than in new car parks. The McAnany Avenue consultation drew four responses, two for and two against, and the council said a resident permit scheme would be needed to guarantee residents a space [9]. Temple Park got new card-only and PayByPhone machines at 1 pound all day [8]. The report names Pierhead as the highest earner, with 292 spaces and 130,154 pounds of tariff income in 2024-25, ahead of South Promenade South with 129 spaces; total off-street tariff income rose from 1,132,846 to 1,334,286 pounds [1].

For electric vehicles, the council announced a planned 20-year partnership with Connected Kerb in December 2023 for 2,000 charge points, replacing all 59 old units [14]. By November 2024 chargers had been installed in five car parks, and rapid charging points at 14 locations were to be upgraded; the council said it was the only North East authority not yet charging for EV charging [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The council runs the car parks itself. The 2024-25 report also lists free car parks in South Shields, Hebburn, Jarrow, Whitburn and Boldon, though its text and table disagree on their number and total, so we do not give them [0]. On the Metro, Travel North East lists free car parks at Hebburn (70 spaces), Fellgate (52) and East Boldon (64), but its pages contradict themselves on several counts and Jarrow is given as 80 spaces in the text and 38 in the table [12]. Heworth, in Gateshead, is run by Gateshead Council [13].

Our data cover two Metro park-and-rides, East Boldon (75 in the feed) and Fellgate (54), with 129 spaces, measured since 25 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 46% on weekdays and 35% at weekends, weighted by spaces. East Boldon is the fuller at 59% on weekdays and reached full in a single Saturday-evening reading; Fellgate averaged 28%. We have no live data for the seafront and town-centre car parks that earn the revenue. These are about four weeks of data.
